cards.title: Task timing was off in some recordings
cards.wrong: The published task intervals (when belt speed or slope changes) were timed on the belt-speed record, not on the motion data. In 4 of 50 treadmill recordings that clock is off by 1.7 to 7 s, and 2 more cannot be checked, so strides near a change can carry the wrong task label.
cards.how: We lined up the belt-speed record with the belt speed measured from heel and toe markers. 44 recordings agree within half a second.
cards.example: AB09 at 10° incline: the best shift is 6.85 s, and the belt-speed error drops from 0.67 to 0.07 m/s at that shift, so the recording is left out. AB01 at 5° incline is an exact copy of its 10° incline recording and is also left out.

cards.title: Joint angles are measured from markers against gravity
cards.short: All 44 recordings; angle columns missing in 83 strides
cards.wrong: The source's own joint angles carry the zero position of the motion-capture software, and that zero is not published. In three recordings probed before the rebuild, the median difference between the published ankle and the ankle from markers was 0.3 to 6.5° and changed with the leg and the trial, so it is not one constant that could be subtracted.
cards.how: Thigh, shank and foot angles come from the markers, each in that leg's own side-view plane and measured from gravity (straight down for thigh and shank, forward horizontal for the foot). Hip, knee and ankle angles are differences of these: hip is thigh minus pelvis, knee is thigh minus shank, ankle is foot minus shank. A second implementation recomputed 16 legs and 176 leg-columns of angles and speeds: the largest difference was 0.0 rad and the pattern of missing values was identical.
cards.did: All hip, knee, ankle, thigh, shank and foot angles in this version are computed this way, and the foot angle and its speed are now released. Nothing is filled in: where a needed marker is not visible, or the pelvis differs from the pelvis from markers by more than 1°, that stride's angle columns are missing (83 strides in 8 recordings). One stride whose leg plane swung more than 60° from the walking direction has its plane-dependent columns held (1 stride, already empty).
cards.example: AB06 at 5° incline: the published ankle sat 4.7° (right leg) and 6.1° (left leg) from the ankle from markers at the median.
cards.total_line: All 44 recordings, 7,545 strides in the full version: every angle column is computed from markers.

cards.title: The knee marker names are reversed in the source
cards.wrong: In this source the marker named KNEM lies on the outer (lateral) side of the knee and KNE on the inner (medial) side. That is the reverse of the usual reading of the names. Each leg's side-view plane is built from the knee axis, so the assignment matters.
cards.how: For every leg we measured how far each marker sits outward from the middle of the pelvis, along the line between the two front hip markers. In 14 legs of 7 recordings, checked independently, KNEM sat 0.117 to 0.141 m further out than KNE and was nearer the thigh markers in every leg. Across all 88 legs the build found the outer marker at least 0.110 m beyond the inner one. The ankle markers are named the usual way, 0.072 to 0.087 m apart.
cards.did: The side-view plane is built with KNEM as the lateral marker and KNE as the medial marker. Nothing else was changed for it. The reversal is written in the package's list of limitations.
cards.example: Across the 14 legs checked independently, the typical outward distance was 0.13 to 0.20 m for KNEM and 0.006 to 0.061 m for KNE.

cards.title: Joint power is recomputed as moment times joint speed
cards.short: All 44 recordings; old gap 12% hip, 9% knee, 15% ankle
cards.wrong: The source's powers do not equal the published moment times the joint speed, and their sign could not be settled from the source alone. Against the moment times our new joint speed, the source's power differed per stride by a median of 12% (hip), 9% (knee) and 15% (ankle) of the size of the new power; for the larger gaps (90th percentile) 27%, 18% and 24%.
cards.how: Per stride, the gap is the square root of the summed squared difference between the source's power and the new power, divided by the square root of the summed squared new power, over the samples where both exist. The median is over strides.
cards.did: Hip, knee and ankle power are now the published moment times our own joint speed: hip is the thigh speed minus the pelvis speed, knee is the thigh speed minus the shank speed (flexion positive), and ankle is the foot speed minus the shank speed. The source's power values are not carried over. Power is missing wherever the moment or a speed is missing. The 1,407 power entries once held back for an unsettled sign are gone, and 174 entries now record power as missing. After the change the gap is zero.
cards.checked: A separate readback of every row found power equal to moment times speed to 1e-12 and 29 other columns identical to the earlier version. An independent check of 10 strides drawn with a recorded seed agreed to better than 1e-9 on every row.
cards.example: Ankle: the median stride differed by 15% before, the largest of the three joints; its zero and definition changed in this version.

cards.title: Pressure point on an estimated plate position, published leg by leg
cards.wrong: The source records the pressure point in each force plate's own frame and does not record where the plate sits in the laboratory. A pressure point in the foot's own frame therefore needs an estimated plate position, and that estimate has to be tested before anyone uses it.
cards.how: The pressure point is expressed in the ankle frame, which turns with the foot, inside that leg's side-view plane; its origin is 100 mm forward of the ankle joint centre along the foot, and sideways is out of the plane. The plate's axis and sign come from the ankle path, its tilt from the belt slope, its forward shift from the hip and knee moments, its height from the rule that the foot rests on the belt, and its sideways shift from the mean foot position.
cards.did: A leg publishes the pressure point only if three checks pass: the ankle moment, held out of the fit, is reproduced (correlation at least 0.95); the toe-off end of the pressure point lies within 4 cm of the toe marker in at least 95% of strides (at 0.2 body weight); and the plate is loaded at the leg's heel strikes in at least 95% of them. Each leg is judged on its own, so a passing leg publishes even when the other leg of the recording is held. 60 of 88 legs pass, and 5,141 strides carry a value. The other 28 legs (2,383 strides) have the three columns present but empty, each with its reason. Published values are labelled 'estimated plate position'.
cards.checked: A second implementation recomputed 16 legs: the unheld pressure point agreed to 7e-16 m and the verdicts were identical. The pass or hold decision of all 88 legs was recomputed from the per-leg numbers: 60 pass, 28 held. Not independent: the plate axis, sign, tilt and shifts were taken from the build's summary.
cards.example: AB01 level: both legs publish (held-out ankle moment correlation 0.998, toe-off within 4 cm in 100% of strides). AB07 at 10° decline: the right leg is held (toe-off within 4 cm in 90% of strides) and the left leg publishes alone.
